_meta.source: Education Criteria for Performance Excellence, 2024-2027 edition (Office of the Permanent Secretary, MHESI) — adapted from the 2023-2024 Baldrige Excellence Framework (Education)
_meta.note: GOVERNING FILE — single source of truth for the EdPEx rubric. The app renders categories/items/scores from this; do not hard-code criteria elsewhere. Points are the OFFICIAL 2567-2570 allocations (cat1=115, cat2=90 — NOT the older 120/85).
_meta.scope_note: Scope of "EdPEx 100%" = completeness against the 'criteria' (Categories/Items/points/OP/core values/ADLI/LeTCI) that the system renders from this file and checks automatically with gates G-01…G-10 — it does not mean that every system-level feature will be delivered in the MVP. MVP = a read-only shell with 100% criteria completeness; entering ADLI/LeTCI scores = Phase B; dashboards tracking the 2024-2027 roadmap / maturity / RACI / HITL = Phase D. See docs/DESIGN-edpex-mvp.md §8 and .docs/EdPEx/_governance/GOVERNANCE-TO-GATES.md.

core_values_detail.name: Systems Perspective
core_values_detail.definition: Manage all parts of the organization as a unified whole to achieve the mission and move toward the vision — plans, processes, measures, and actions are aligned and work together.
core_values_detail.design: Link Items and Categories explicitly; do not store Items as isolated islands.

core_values_detail.name: Visionary Leadership
core_values_detail.definition: Senior leaders set the vision, create a customer focus, demonstrate values and ethics, and set high expectations.
core_values_detail.design: Category 1 stores the deployment of mission/vision/values as evidence, linked to strategic objectives (Category 2).

core_values_detail.name: Student-Focused Excellence
core_values_detail.definition: Considers the features of programs/services, access and support channels, and all values/behaviors that create value for customers/students.
core_values_detail.design: Students/stakeholders are the core entities; Category 3 + 7.2 form a complete loop: listen → needs → results.

core_values_detail.name: Valuing People
core_values_detail.definition: Success depends on an engaged workforce with meaningful work, learning, and accountability, including partners.
core_values_detail.design: Category 5 links engagement drivers → results (7.3); workforce data can be segmented.

core_values_detail.name: Organizational Agility and Resilience
core_values_detail.definition: The ability to change/adapt rapidly + to anticipate, prepare for, and recover from disruptions.
core_values_detail.design: Supports versioned reassessment, tracking of plan adjustments, and risk/continuity fields in Category 6.

core_values_detail.name: Organizational Learning
core_values_detail.definition: Continuously improve existing approaches + breakthrough innovation, leading to new goals/approaches/services.
core_values_detail.design: The L dimension of ADLI must be an actually stored field (evaluation/improvement/sharing cycle), not implicit.

core_values_detail.name: Focus on Success and Innovation
core_values_detail.definition: Understand the short- and long-term factors affecting the organization, and drive innovation.
core_values_detail.design: Category 2 has two planning time horizons (short/long); innovation is a taggable type of improvement.

core_values_detail.name: Management by Fact
core_values_detail.definition: Measure and analyze performance both internally and against the competitive environment.
core_values_detail.design: Every answer/claim must be tied to evidence and be measurable — evidence attachment + mandatory measures (prime directive).

core_values_detail.name: Societal Contribution
core_values_detail.definition: Leaders prioritize the public good and societal well-being, and serve as role models in health, safety, and the environment.
core_values_detail.design: Societal responsibility Items in Category 1.2 + results 7.4; community/legal/ethics fields.

core_values_detail.name: Ethics and Transparency
core_values_detail.definition: Behave ethically in all interactions with stakeholders; leaders serve as role models with clear expectations.
core_values_detail.design: Audit trail + ethics/governance Items (1.2) with results (7.4); transparency = visible change history.

core_values_detail.name: Delivering Value and Results
core_values_detail.definition: Select/analyze the results delivered and balance value for stakeholders — not just financial.
core_values_detail.design: Category 7 results series cover 7.1–7.5 (balanced scorecard, not a single measure).

method.systems_perspective: Manage all components as a unified whole — the OP is the overarching context at the top · Category 4 (Measurement/Analysis/Knowledge) is the foundation (the brain) · the leadership triad (1→2,3) feeds the results triad (5,6→7) through the Integration core
characteristics: Non-prescriptive — asks 'how/what'; adaptable to any organization
Systems perspective — view the organization as one interconnected machine, not 7 silos
Applicable at any level of maturity (any point on its journey)
Results-oriented — processes drive results; results feed back into improvement
Promotes learning and continuous cycles of improvement (cycles of improvement)

how_what.process: Categories 1–6 ask "how do you do it" (processes — scored with ADLI)
how_what.results: Category 7 asks "what are the results" (results — scored with LeTCI)

response_guidelines: Answer specifically and measurably; do not narrate events/minor anecdotes.
Always tie answers to the OP and the organizational context.
Every answer has ≥ 1 piece of evidence and a measure (Management by Fact).
Results (Category 7) must have time series and comparisons (Trends + Comparisons).
Identify strengths and opportunities for improvement (OFIs) for every Item.
method.op_framing: The OP is the first self-assessment and the context that shapes every answer in Categories 1–7 — conflicting or missing OP information is a signal for improvement planning from the outset.

items.title: Educational Programs, Research, and Other Educational Services
items.guide: What are the institution's main educational programs, research, and services? What is their comparative importance (including percentage of revenue/budget) to the institution's success, and by what methods does the institution deliver them?

items.title: Mission, Vision, Values, and Culture
items.guide: What are the institution's mission, vision, and values? What are the distinctive characteristics of its organizational culture? What are its core competencies, and how do they relate to the mission and vision?

items.title: Workforce Profile
items.guide: What is the overall profile of the workforce, including faculty and staff groups/categories, key engagement drivers, and significant changes in workforce capability, capacity, and composition?

items.title: Assets
items.guide: What are the institution's key assets, such as facilities, equipment, technology, and intellectual property?

items.title: Regulatory Environment
items.guide: What are the key standards and requirements, accreditations, certifications, or registration requirements that the institution applies?

items.title: Organizational Structure
items.guide: What are the leadership and governance structures of the organization? What are the key components of the leadership system, and what are the reporting relationships among the governing board, senior leaders, and the parent organization?

items.title: Students, Other Customers, and Stakeholders
items.guide: What are the key market segments, students, other customers, and stakeholders? What are their key needs and expectations for educational programs, research, and services, and how do the groups differ?

items.title: Suppliers, Formal and Informal Partners
items.guide: How many types of key suppliers and formal and informal partners are there, and what are they? What role does each group play in delivering programs/services and in implementing innovation, and what are the key requirements of the supply network?

items.title: Competitive Position
items.guide: What are the size, share, and growth of the education sector or market in which the institution operates? How many competitors are there and of what types? What differentiates the institution from its competitors, both nationally and internationally?

items.title: Changes in Competitiveness
items.guide: What key changes affect the institution's competitive situation, including changes that create opportunities for collaboration and innovation?

items.title: Comparative Data
items.guide: What are the key sources of comparative and competitive data, both within and outside the education sector, and what limitations does the institution face in obtaining or using these data?

items.title: Key Strategic Challenges (Educational, Operational, Societal Responsibility, and Workforce)
items.guide: What are the institution's key strategic challenges and threats, covering educational programs, operations, societal responsibility, and the workforce?

items.title: Key Strategic Advantages (Educational, Operational, Societal Responsibility, and Workforce)
items.guide: What are the institution's key strategic advantages and strategic opportunities, covering educational programs, operations, societal responsibility, and the workforce?

items.title: Performance Improvement System
items.guide: What are the institution's overall performance improvement systems, including evaluation tools and processes, organizational learning, and innovation?

scoring.gate_rule: Assess holistically, not by averaging individual factors: choose the band that best reflects the overall picture, then choose a sub-value (percent) within that band. The weakest dimension acts as a Gate that prevents moving up to a higher band. Store both band and percent; item_score = percent × item.points. (Criteria p. 79)
scoring.percent_choices_note: Each band is a 'set' of selectable % values (the choices field), not a continuous range — the system must enforce selection only from values in choices.

ADLI.name: Approach-Deployment-Learning-Integration
ADLI.source: Process scoring range table, PDF p. 80

bands.label: Reactive
bands.desc: A: No systematic approach; answers are narrative. D: None/very little. L: No improvement concept; adjusts when problems arise. I: No alignment; each unit works independently.

bands.label: Early systematic
bands.desc: A: Beginning to have a systematic approach that answers basic questions. D: Beginning deployment; obstacles remain. L: Beginning to shift from reactive to basic improvement. I: Beginning to align through joint problem solving.

bands.label: Systematic, beginning deployment
bands.desc: A: Has a systematic approach that answers basic questions. D: Deployed, although some units are just beginning. L: Beginning to have approaches to evaluate/improve key processes. I: Beginning to align with basic needs per the OP.

bands.label: Systematic, deployed, learning
bands.desc: A: Has a systematic approach that answers the questions overall. D: Well deployed, although some units are just beginning. L: Systematic evaluation/improvement using real data + beginning innovation. I: Aligned with overall needs per the OP.

bands.label: Systematic, integrated
bands.desc: A: Systematic; answers most sub-questions. D: Well deployed with no significant differences. L: Systematic evaluation/improvement + learning; demonstrates innovation. I: Integrated per the OP, both now and in the future.

bands.label: Role model
bands.desc: A: Systematic; answers all sub-questions completely. D: Deployed thoroughly with no weaknesses. L: Improvement + innovation are institution-level tools. I: Fully integrated per the OP.

LeTCI.name: Levels-Trends-Comparisons-Integration
LeTCI.source: Results scoring range table, PDF p. 81

bands.label: No or few results
bands.desc: Le: None/poor in the areas reported. T: No trends/negative trends. C: No comparative information. I: No results in areas important to the mission.

bands.label: Some results
bands.desc: Le: Reported for some areas; beginning to show good levels. T: Beginning to show trends/negative trends in some areas. C: Almost no comparisons. I: Results in only some important areas.

bands.label: Results with trends
bands.desc: Le: Good levels that answer basic questions. T: Good trends in important areas. C: Beginning to have comparative information. I: Results in many areas important to the mission.

bands.label: Good trends, beginning benchmarking
bands.desc: Le: Good levels that answer the questions overall. T: Sustained good trends. C: Beginning to compare with comparable organizations/benchmark levels. I: Covers most important students/customers/processes.

bands.label: Good results, benchmarkable, integrated
bands.desc: Le: Very good levels that answer most sub-questions. T: Sustained in important areas. C: Good benchmarking; leader in many areas. I: Covers most needs.

bands.label: Leader, high-level benchmarking
bands.desc: Le: Excellent; answers all sub-questions completely. T: Sustained; leader. C: Leader within the benchmark sector. I: Covers + projects results for most students/customers/workforce/market/processes/action plans.
